prompt: By comparing the kinetic theory equation pV = (1/3) N m <c^2> with the ideal gas equation pV = NkT, what expression is deduced for the average translational kinetic energy E_K of a gas molecule?

answer.explanation: Equating (1/3) N m <c^2> = NkT gives (1/3) m <c^2> = kT. Multiplying both sides by 3/2 yields (1/2) m <c^2> = (3/2) kT, so E_K = (3/2) kT.

distractor_explanations: Option 2 is incorrect: (1/2) kT is the energy per degree of freedom, but 3D translational motion has 3 degrees of freedom.
Option 3 is incorrect: 3 kT forgets to multiply by 1/2 when converting m <c^2> to (1/2) m <c^2>.
Option 4 is incorrect: this is the inverted fraction 2/3.
hints: Equate the right-hand sides of pV = (1/3) N m <c^2> and pV = NkT.
Rearrange the equation to isolate (1/2) m <c^2>.
solution:
Equating the two expressions for pV:
(1/3) N m <c^2> = NkT
Divide by N:
(1/3) m <c^2> = kT
Multiply by 3/2:
(1/2) m <c^2> = (3/2) kT
Since E_K = (1/2) m <c^2>, E_K = (3/2) kT. Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Write pV = (1/3) N m <c^2> and pV = NkT side by side.
Emphasize that this proves thermodynamic temperature T is directly proportional to average translational kinetic energy.
